recommendation: Prioritize completing and reviewing the already-running full repair: this has a more defensible physical distinction than the held-control pilot, and no exact ferrule-replacement duplicate was found in this narrow review. Do not automatically clear novelty from the successful lift check or from the repaired-object label. Final source-matched review should evaluate the complete weakest valid route and explicitly accept or reject the remaining overlap with generic rubber-sleeve fitting.
scope: Submission-focused narrow review of specified nearby tasks, accepted replacement/release tasks, current guarded scorer and proposed metadata. No new simulation, task edits, claim edits or novelty-gate stamp.

candidate_files.obsolete_canonical: Current task.py/task.json are development entries; do not bind a submission novelty gate to them.

physical_skill: Extract an installed worn-through rubber foot without a fixture, manage a loose full-size crutch, align and push its22mm shaft into a matching dry rubber replacement to the sole stop, then handle the assembly without the foot falling off.
weakest_valid_route: Remove worn foot while using any ordinary available bench or hand counter-support.
Regrasp and orient the native crutch; push its shaft into the spare already standing on its sole. The spare need not be picked up or held.
Lift so the foot is unsupported and verify that it remains seated; return assembly to the bench and release.
valid_shortcuts: Bench reaction may provide insertion resistance; no spare grasp is required.
Straight push without twist is valid if it seats; manufacturer says slight twisting may help, not that it is mandatory.
One or two arms, any safe grasp ordering, native handgrip or shaft grasp, and ordinary non-destructive environmental support remain valid.
Recoverable drops can be repaired; do not create an arbitrary arm sequence or irreversible failure merely to enforce difficulty.
distinct_from_nearest: The complete operation replaces an already fitted worn consumable on a freely handled full-size assistive device. The physical work includes overcoming the old dry sleeve fit and seating the compatible new one while controlling the long unfixed assembly. The nearest#793 starts with separate parts and a permanently fixed short glass tube; its central safety skill is close glass support during stopper manipulation. These are meaningful task-level differences, but both assembly stages reduce to coaxial rubber interference fitting under the easiest valid bench route.
residual_risk: Removal plus reinsertion can be read as concatenated familiar pull/push primitives; accepted#800 already includes worn-part replacement, and#662 already includes tube extraction.
The upright spare removes loose-spare acquisition and counterholding from the assembly step. Do not claim those as essential difficulty.
Full scale and free-body handling preserve the real operation, but size/layout alone do not establish novelty; the final video must show the complete repair rather than a pre-seated component.
Visible wear and a fall-risk story are meaningful context; classification/diagnosis alone can be tested without a robot.
Friction-based retention and stronger physical modeling improve construct validity, not automatically the distinct skill.
Own-weight retention is roughly a0.49N foot-weight check; it does not establish patient load capacity, slip resistance or general clinical readiness.

nearest_prs.operation: Fit a rubber stopper onto a fixed short glass tube while maintaining close protective support.
nearest_prs.comparison: Shared interference-fit push/twist primitive. Crutch additionally needs extraction of the installed worn foot and handling/reorientation of a free90cm assembly; #793 instead centres on protecting fragile glass through prescribed nearby support. Neither different material nor superior contact fidelity alone is novel. Its latest task/source uses a captured coaxial sliding/rotating fit joint after seating.
nearest_prs.implication: Material overlap, not an established exact duplicate.

nearest_prs.operation: Identify and remove a worn gripper finger, fit a new one under a fork plate and place three screws.
nearest_prs.comparison: Worn-part recognition and replacement are already represented. Crutch lacks that task's screws/plate manipulation but adds an actual frictional extraction and interference-fit operation on an unfixed full-size aid.
nearest_prs.implication: Do not pitch visual wear recognition or swap sequence alone as new.

nearest_prs.operation: Hold a release collet depressed while extracting pipe from a push-fit connector.
nearest_prs.comparison: Tube extraction is represented, but released collet locking differs from pulling a dry rubber sleeve off an aluminum tube. Crutch has no collet-release interlock and must also install the replacement.
nearest_prs.implication: Different mechanism; does not make generic pulling inherently novel.

nearest_prs.operation: Replace a blade in a quick-release holder and verify retention.
nearest_prs.comparison: Rejected for weak real-world relevance despite replacement and retention check. Crutch has a concrete worn-foot hazard backed by manufacturer fitting guidance; the verification stage alone supplies no novelty.
nearest_prs.implication: Retention cannot rescue an otherwise generic repair claim.

nearest_prs.comparison: Same assistive object, different operation. Rejection was category relevance, not an exhaustive prohibition on crutch tasks. Current category must rest on the visible worn-through foot and slip hazard, not general familiarity or an occupation count.
nearest_prs.implication: Not a physical duplicate; category claim needs precise scope.

nearest_prs.operation: Adjust miniature fixed walking-stick stand-in using bayonet slots.
nearest_prs.comparison: Full-size free crutch and actual friction interface avoid the cited miniaturization/substituted-mechanism issue. Correct fidelity is necessary, not sufficient novelty.
nearest_prs.implication: Useful construct-validity precedent, not novelty clearance.

nearest_prs.operation: Replace worn squeegee rubber by threading a long floppy strip through its channel and fitting end clips.
nearest_prs.comparison: Shares replacing worn elastomer; defining manipulation is flexible-strip routing and clipping, not radial sleeve interference.

nearest_prs.operation: Match and place ground-glass stoppers in flasks.
nearest_prs.comparison: Shows that recognizing the right part plus ordinary placement may fail importance. Crutch requires removal and frictional seating rather than just a drop-in cone; force calibration remains an estimate.
nearest_prs.implication: Warns against relying on semantic matching or object label.

nearest_prs.operation: Seat a swing-top stopper and close over-centre bail.
nearest_prs.comparison: Exact closure mechanism was already pending elsewhere. It is not the crutch mechanism.
nearest_prs.implication: Benchmark compares physical skill, not just labels or improved implementation.

submission_framing.supportable: Repair a visibly worn-through foot on a full-size loose crutch by removing it and fully seating the compatible replacement. Real fitting operation with physical retention, no clamp or attachment latch.
avoid: Novel because a lift/retention test is required.
Must counterhold the spare with the other hand.
Must twist, use two arms, or follow the demonstrated regrasp sequence.
Patient-safe, load-certified, or ready for weight bearing after an own-weight check.
Higher simulation fidelity than#793 is itself a new physical skill.
submission_framing.category: Safety and alignment is defensible as a worn-through-foot slip-hazard recovery, provided the text states the limited fitting/retention scope and does not claim actual clinical certification.

metadata_review.scoring_scope: Removal alone earns no credit. Partial requires seated replacement and observed unsupported retention. Full requires assembly returned and released. Arm assignment is not scored.
metadata_review.remaining: Proposed scoring text needs a concise real-observation equivalent before submission; contact-sensor tolerances and coordinate sampling details are implementation evidence, not by themselves a human scoring procedure. Final source/canonical promotion, complete demonstration, model/media and normal submission checks remain owner/root responsibilities.

manufacturer_evidence.finding: Manufacturer describes removing an existing worn ferrule by pulling, optionally twisting; fitting surfaces must be clean and dry; push replacement until further travel stops, optionally twist. It warns against oils/lubricants. Thus ordinary axial pull/push and bench-supported insertion should remain legitimate; twisting is not a mandated distinct skill.
